NEW DELHI: Two of Punjab's oldest political allies are back together, six years after a bitter parting over the contentious farm laws. The Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) and the Shiromani Akali Dal ( SAD ) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections , reviving a partnership that once governed the state for 15 years across three terms.The reunion, announced on the Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, brings together parties whose relationship was famously described by former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal as "nau-maas da rishta", the bond between the nail and the flesh.Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the development, saying the alliance would put Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first."Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress," he said in a post on X, adding that the partnership, nurtured by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, LK Advani and Parkash Singh Badal, had "stood the test of time".Union home minister Amit Shah, who announced the reunion alongside BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, called the Akali Dal the NDA's "oldest ally" and said PM Modi had described the development by saying the "NDA is now complete".Shah also said SAD would retain its senior-partner status, adding that the "big brother" would get the chief minister's post. "Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats.Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," the Union minister said at the joint press conference.The two parties will contest all 117 assembly seats together, although the seat-sharing arrangement is yet to be finalised.The reunion comes after months of political manoeuvring, including Sukhbir Badal's meeting with PM Modi in August and a shift in SAD's position on the Centre's delimitation proposal. It also brings together two parties whose electoral fortunes have declined sharply since their separation.However, Punjab is no longer the state in which the old alliance enjoyed its strongest run. AAP has emerged as the dominant force, Congress remains a significant contender, and the BJP and SAD have both undergone changes in their support bases and political strategies.The partnership actually predates the BJP. Its predecessor, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, shared power with the Akalis in Punjab as far back as 1967 and 1969. The modern alliance, however, was forged in 1996, when SAD's Moga Declaration pivoted from purely Panthic politics to a broader pitch of "Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat."The partnership brought together the Akalis' predominantly rural Sikh support base and the BJP's largely urban Hindu constituency. It also helped both parties build a political coalition in the aftermath of militancy in Punjab.The alliance won 93 of 117 assembly seats in 1997, with SAD securing 75 and the BJP 18. After losing power to Congress in 2002, the combine returned to office in 2007 and retained power in 2012, winning 67 and 68 seats respectively.But the emergence of AAP, coupled with public anger over incidents of sacrilege and the drug menace, weakened the alliance. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three.The final rupture came in September 2020, when SAD walked out of the NDA over the Centre's three farm laws. Sukhbir Badal's wife Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned as Union food processing industries minister on September 17, and the Akali Dal formally ended its 24-year-old electoral partnership with the BJP nine days later.The laws were repealed in November 2021, but the political damage endured.The alliance's decline is evident from its electoral record. In 2007, SAD won 48 seats and the BJP 19, taking their combined tally to 67. They improved to 68 seats in 2012, with SAD winning 56 and the BJP 12. But the numbers fell sharply thereafter. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three. By the 2022 assembly elections, the two parties managed just five seats between them, with SAD winning three and the BJP two.In 2022, SAD secured 18.38% of the vote and the BJP 6.60%, while AAP swept the election with 92 seats and a 42.01% vote share.Their separate performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections provided another reason to reconsider the alliance. The BJP failed to win any of Punjab's 13 seats despite securing 18.56% of the vote. SAD won one seat, Bathinda, with 13.42%.Together, their vote shares added up to nearly 32%, compared with 26.30% for Congress and 26.02% for AAP.The numbers make a case for pooling their support bases, although the combined vote share does not automatically translate into transferable votes or assembly seats.For the BJP, the alliance offers access to SAD's traditional rural and Sikh support networks. For the Akali Dal, it brings back a national ally and an opportunity to rebuild its electoral machinery, which is the BJP's strong suit.Sukhbir Singh Badal described the reunion as more than an electoral arrangement."This is not just a political alliance. There is an emotional bond. As my late father used to say, Akali Dal-BJP is an inseparable, deeply bonded relationship," he said.The old partners are back again, but the state the BJP and SAD are returning to is markedly different from the one they left behind in 2020.The 2027 assembly election will be the alliance's first major state-level electoral test without Parkash Singh Badal, the five-time CM who died in April 2023. A towering figure in the Akali Dal, he was also a key bridge between the SAD and the BJP. Though Sukhbir Badal was already leading the party before his father's death, he now has to rebuild the party's standing without his political stature and influence.Another factor the alliance must keep in mind is that the farm issue has not disappeared. The repeal of the three farm laws did not automatically undo the distrust they created. Farmers' demands, including a legal guarantee for minimum support price, remain unresolved, keeping the issue politically alive in an agrarian state like Punjab. The BJP-SAD alliance will have to reckon with that trust deficit, particularly in the rural Malwa belt, which is the largest and most populous region covering major farming districts like Bathinda, Mansa, Sangrur, Patiala, Ludhiana and Muktsar.This is why the choice of Gurpurab for the reunion announcement is rich in symbolism. PM Modi had announced the repeal of the farm laws on the occasion in November 2021. The two parties have now chosen the same religious occasion to announce their political reconciliation. Whether that symbolism can translate into renewed trust among farmers is a different question.Another thing that has changed is that the Akali Dal can no longer assume that it commands the entire Panthic vote. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, independent candidates Amritpal Singh and Sarabjeet Singh Khalsa won from Khadoor Sahib and Faridkot, respectively. Between them, they also led in 15 assembly segments.This makes the party's return to its traditional Panthic space more difficult. The SAD has tried to reconnect with its core constituency through issues of Sikh identity and historical memory. The controversy surrounding 'Satluj', a film based on activist Jaswant Singh Khalra's work documenting alleged extrajudicial killings in Punjab, offered one such opportunity. After the film was taken down from an OTT platform, Sukhbir Badal announced screenings across the state, saying young people should know about the events it depicts.Six years on its own have transformed the BJP from a junior partner that contested just 23 of Punjab's 117 assembly seats into a more assertive player. Under the old arrangement, the SAD contested 94 assembly seats and the BJP 23, largely in urban constituencies. For the Lok Sabha elections, the split was 10 seats for the Akalis and three for the BJP.Its vote share in the 2024 Lok Sabha election rose to 18.56 per cent, up from 9.63 per cent in 2019. The BJP contested all 13 seats in 2024, compared with just three under the old seat-sharing arrangement in 2019. Though it won no seats, the saffron party's vote share was higher than the SAD's 13.42 per cent. In the 2022 assembly election, the BJP had polled 6.60 per cent and won two seats.The party has also strengthened its ranks through a steady stream of defections. In April 2026, AAP Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha led six other MPs into the BJP which included Sandeep Pathak, Ashok Mittal, Harbhajan Singh, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Rajinder Gupta and Swati Maliwal. Six of these seven were Rajya Sabha members from Punjab. The exits dealt a major blow to the AAP's parliamentary strength and brought into the BJP leaders who had been closely associated with the party's Punjab strategy. Chadha and Pathak, in particular, had played key roles in the AAP's political and electoral planning.The BJP has since moved to put these former AAP leaders to work against their old party. Chadha and Harbhajan Singh have been named to its Punjab manifesto committee, while Pathak, Mittal, Sahney and other former AAP MPs have been assigned roles in the party's chargesheet committee, which will prepare its case against the Bhagwant Mann government.Earlier, in March 2024, AAP's then Jalandhar MP Sushil Kumar Rinku and Jalandhar West MLA Sheetal Angural had also joined the BJP. In November 2026, three more AAP legislators, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, crossed over. The BJP has also inducted senior Akali leaders, including Surinder Singh Chauhan and Jaswinderpal Sohal, as well as AAP functionaries from Moga led by spokesperson Navdeep Singh Sangha.The BJP's recruitment drive has not been limited to the AAP and SAD. Its Punjab ranks also include former Congress leaders such as Sunil Jakhar, Manpreet Singh Badal, Ravneet Singh Bittu and Preneet Kaur.That changes the terms of the reunion. The BJP returns with a larger vote share, a wider organisational footprint and experienced leaders. The SAD, meanwhile, needs the alliance to recover lost ground and reconnect with rural voters. Amit Shah has announced that the BJP is okay with the junior-partner label in the alliance. It is, however, unlikely that the BJP will settle for the old seat-sharing formula.The immediate target of the alliance is the AAP government, which swept to power in 2022 with 92 seats and 42.01 per cent of the vote. Its vote share fell to 26.02 per cent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when it won three seats, but it remains a formidable player.The SAD-BJP reunion gives the opposition a potentially stronger combination of urban and rural networks. It could also help consolidate voters who want an alternative to the AAP government. The drug problem, in particular, is likely to be a central campaign issue.At his press conference, Amit Shah listed three priorities for a future NDA government: eliminating drugs, eliminating corruption and strengthening nationalist forces. He promised that Punjab would be "completely drug-free" by December 31, 2029. He also targeted Congress, recalling Rahul Gandhi's 2017 promise that drugs would be eliminated within one term and accusing the party of doing nothing when it was in power.The attack gives the alliance a ready-made campaign plank. But it also puts the BJP and SAD on the spot, as both parties have been part of Punjab's political establishment for decades. The voters, thus, will judge their record as well as their promises.There is another complication. The Congress remains a strong third front and could split the anti-incumbency vote. Rural Sikh voters who continue to view the BJP through the lens of the farm agitation may also be reluctant to back the reunited partners. The AAP could benefit if opposition votes remain divided.The BJP-SAD reunion also complicates the Congress's position. With an established opposition pole, the contest for voters dissatisfied with the AAP government will now intensify. Amit Shah's attack on the Congress over its record on drugs made it clear that the alliance intends to take on both the ruling party and its principal rival.The Congress can still draw on its independent support base, but it will have to navigate a more crowded opposition space, as well as its own internal factional differences.Six years after a split that left both allies on the margins, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal have chosen pragmatism over past grievances to challenge AAP and Congress. The 2027 election, however, will not be a simple replay of the coalition's past victories. And tough seat-sharing talks are yet to be held.The OGs may be back together, but winning over a changed Punjab will require more than old chemistry.
Article Summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) and the Shiromani Akali Dal ( SAD ) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections. The two parties will contest all 117 assembly seats together, although the seat-sharing arrangement is yet to be finalised. The reunion comes after months of political manoeuvring.

Article Title: NSA Ajit Doval, Maldives defence minister discuss security ties at Colombo meet
Article Text:
NSA Ajit Doval met Maldives' minister of defence and national service Hassan Rasheed on the sidelines of the eighth Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) NSA-level meeting

NEW DELHI: National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval called on Maldives defence minister Hassan Rasheed on the sidelines of the 8th Colombo Security Conclave meeting and discussed ways to strengthen defence and security cooperation between the two countries.This was the first high-level contact between the two countries after President Mohamed Muizzu's visit to Pakistan recently. That visit raised eyebrows here as Maldives signed 20 MoUs with Pakistan, including in areas like defence and maritime cooperation. Muizzu had also called for the resumption of the Saarc summit process during his visit.Doval is in Male for the CSC, which was formed to promote closer cooperation between member states on vital matters of security and to strengthen partnerships for enhancing regional security in the Indian Ocean Region.Originally launched in 2011 as a trilateral maritime security dialogue involving India, Sri Lanka and the Maldives, the grouping later inducted Mauritius, Bangladesh, and Seychelles into its fold.
Article Summary: National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval called on Maldives defence minister Hassan Rasheed on the sidelines of the 8th Colombo Security Conclave meeting. This was the first high-level contact between the two countries after President Mohamed Muizzu's visit to Pakistan recently.

NEW DELHI: An Iranian delegation met officials from the ministry of external affairs (MEA) in New Delhi on Wednesday to discuss multilateral cooperation under the framework of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA).According to news agency ANI, the Iranian delegation was led by Alireza Tootonchian, director general for multilateral and International economic cooperation. He met Thelma John David, MEA joint secretary (Indo-Pacific), in the national capital. Both sides exchanged views on strengthening cooperation through the regional grouping.In a post on X, the Iranian embassy in India said that Tootonchian and deputy director general Abolfazl Azizi Panah held discussions with David on multilateral cooperation under the IORA framework.The meeting comes ahead of the 25th IORA Council of Ministers meeting, scheduled to take place in New Delhi on Friday. Foreign ministers from member countries are expected to attend the gathering to discuss regional cooperation and strategic priorities in the Indian Ocean Region.India is also hosting the 29th IORA Committee of Senior Officials (CSO) meeting ahead of the ministerial gathering. The two-day meeting began on Wednesday.The council of ministers is IORA's highest decision-making body and comprises foreign ministers of member states. It provides strategic and policy direction to the association, reviews progress in regional cooperation and identifies new areas of collaboration.The committee of senior officials is the organisation's second-highest decision-making body. It comprises senior government representatives who oversee the implementation of ministerial decisions, review recommendations and coordinate IORA's work programmes.Meanwhile, the European union (EU) and IORA held their first high-level roundtable on maritime security in New Delhi on Tuesday. Representatives from several Indian Ocean countries participated in discussions on improving maritime surveillance, tackling piracy and trafficking, and protecting important shipping routes.The European union organised the event with support from its project 'Enhancing the EU's security cooperation in and with Asia and the Indo-Pacific' (ESIWA+) and in coordination with its Delegation to India.Addressing the gathering, EU ambassador to India Jean-Eric Paquet reaffirmed the bloc's commitment to expanding security and defence cooperation with regional partners. He also stressed the importance of sharing information to tackle maritime threats.Paquet said maritime security was a shared priority for the EU and IORA, adding that regional cooperation was essential to addressing maritime crime and other challenges at sea.He also highlighted the Indian ocean's importance to global trade, warning that maritime insecurity could disrupt international supply chains and affect economic growth across the region.Representatives from IORA member states and dialogue partners, including India, Australia, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Mauritius, Mozambique, Seychelles and Saudi Arabia, attended the roundtable.Participants discussed improving maritime domain awareness, strengthening policy dialogue and expanding cooperation through EU-supported initiatives such as EUCRIMARIO, EnMAR+ and ESIWA+.The discussions also covered the European Union naval force's operation ATALANTA, which works to improve maritime security in the western Indian ocean and red sea. The operation focuses on deterring piracy, protecting vulnerable vessels and monitoring illegal maritime activities.India assumed the IORA chairmanship from Sri Lanka in November 2025 for the 2025-2027 term. Its chairmanship theme is "innovation, openness, resilience and adaptability in the Indian ocean region".
Article Summary: Iranian delegation meets officials from India's Ministry of External Affairs. Both sides exchanged views on strengthening cooperation through the regional grouping. Meeting comes ahead of the 25th IORA Council of Ministers meeting, scheduled to take place in New Delhi on Friday.

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has launched a nationwide surveillance exercise to assess the quality of packaged drinking water, with the results expected to take at least one to two months, FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani said.The exercise is being carried out across the country as part of the food safety regulator's ongoing efforts to examine various food categories and ensure compliance with prescribed standards."That process has started, and we're doing it across the country. The results will take at least a month or two," Punhani told reporters.He clarified that packaged drinking water was not selected for any specific reason but was part of the regulator's broader surveillance programme."Last year, we took up dairy, meat, eggs, cereals, energy drinks, sugary drinks and other products. So, water is also part of the process," he added.Separately, Punhani stressed the need for food businesses to follow ethical advertising practices, particularly when making claims about their products and promoting them.He emphasised that the regulator was not looking at the issue solely from a legal perspective and urged industry players to consider the ethical dimensions of advertising."The idea is not that it's only the legal part of it. It is also the ethical part of it," he said, calling on the industry to focus on responsible advertising practices.Punhani's remarks and the nationwide surveillance exercise come amid regulatory action against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International over a sample collected from its Goa facility.On November 23, the FSSAI granted sanction to prosecute the company after a regulatory sample was initially found non-compliant with the prescribed limits for bromate and declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.Following an appeal by the company, the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory for further examination, which also declared it unsafe after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).However, the FSSAI clarified on Monday that the action was limited to a single sample from one batch, numbered GO 270, collected from the company's plant at Verna Electronic City in South Goa.The authority also issued an order prohibiting the sale of the concerned batch under Section 36(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act.Bisleri International subsequently welcomed the clarification, maintaining that the sales prohibition applied only to the specific batch manufactured at its Goa plant on September 27, 2025.The company stated that it produces more than 50,000 batches annually and that no stocks of the particular batch were currently available in the market. It also maintained that retesting found bromate levels below the permissible limit.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has launched a nationwide surveillance exercise to assess the quality of packaged drinking water. The exercise is being carried out across the country as part of the food safety regulator's ongoing efforts. The drive comes amid the ongoing Bisleri row.

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Wednesday asked People's Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti not to exploit people's religious sentiments for political gain after she criticised road construction near Sheshnag Lake along the Amarnath pilgrimage route in Jammu and Kashmir 's Anantnag.Jammu and Kashmir BJP chief Sat Sharma said decisions should be based on technical reports and expert assessments rather than political statements."Development based on technical reports should not be politicised, and interference in anyone's religious faith will not be tolerated," Sharma told reporters in Jammu."If a technical report says a building is unsafe or a particular road cannot be constructed, its recommendations must be followed. NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party (SP), accusing its leadership of practising family-centric politics and failing to respect the sentiments of devotees of Lord Ram.“Radhe Radhe is just the beginning. Time for Ram Naam Satya is approaching for the SP,” Adityanath said, taking a swipe at the party during an interview at the ABP Conclave, as cited by news agency PTI.The chief minister also targeted SP president Akhilesh Yadav over his proposed visit to Ayodhya, saying those who tried to sail in two boats would eventually drown.CM Adityanath said the SP leadership should apologise to Ram devotees and Hindus for the firing on devotees in the 1990s. “If the SP leadership had shown some wisdom in the 1990s, bullets would not have been fired at Ram devotees. They should now apologise to Ram devotees and Hindus,” he said, according to a press statement of the interview.Explaining his remark, CM Yogi said greetings should reflect local religious traditions, with 'Radhe Radhe' appropriate in Mathura, 'Jai Shri Ram' in Ayodhya and 'Har Har Mahadev' in Kashi.He added that 'Ram Naam Satya' was traditionally associated with a person's final journey.Taking aim at the SP's PDA slogan, CM Adityanath described it as “Parivar Development Authority”, alleging that the party's politics was limited to the interests of its own family.He also criticised the SP-Congress alliance, claiming it had run into trouble even before the elections because of differences over seat-sharing. The chief minister pointed to the two parties announcing candidates while negotiations were still under way.The seat-sharing discussions have remained inconclusive after two rounds of meetings. The SP announced five candidates on Tuesday, prompting criticism from Congress leaders.Congress's Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said the SP should have waited until the negotiations were over. “They should have avoided that and waited (for the talks to be over),” he told PTI, while expressing hope that the discussions would proceed in the right direction.Congress MP Imran Masood also questioned the SP's move, saying simultaneous talks and candidate announcements suggested that the party was not serious about the negotiations. He said the Congress would consult its leadership on whether discussions should continue.SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, meanwhile, urged the Congress to focus on “winning equations” rather than the number of seats. He asked the party to share a list of constituencies it was interested in contesting beyond the 26 seats proposed by the SP, so that both parties could jointly assess which candidate was best placed to win.Adityanath said the BJP and its National Democratic Alliance allies would contest the elections together, with candidates selected through the party's established process.On the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, CM Adityanath said the exercise was necessary to remove the names of deceased voters and people who had shifted elsewhere.“Every eligible Indian citizen should have a place on the voter list, but a foreign national cannot have voting rights,” he said, accusing the SP of supporting infiltrators while questioning Indian citizens.The chief minister also highlighted what he described as Uttar Pradesh's economic transformation since 2017, saying the state's economy, per capita income and budget had grown more than threefold. He claimed the state had moved from being a “BIMARU” state to a growth engine.Contrasting the state's industrial landscape with that under previous governments, CM Adityanath said Uttar Pradesh had moved from illegal country-made pistol and bomb factories to manufacturing revolvers, rifles and BrahMos missiles.He said the state had received investment proposals worth Rs 50 lakh crore and introduced 36 sector-specific policies to attract investors. Uttar Pradesh, he added, accounted for 55 per cent of India's mobile phone production and 60 per cent of electronic component manufacturing.The chief minister said the micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) sector and the One District One Product (ODOP) initiative were providing employment to 3.25 crore people. He also claimed that housing disputes involving four lakh homebuyers had been resolved through dialogue between builders and buyers.On employment, he said the government had issued nearly 9.75 lakh appointment letters to young people and aimed to increase the number to 10.5 lakh by January 26.Warning those threatening the safety of women, traders and investors, he said people who cast an evil eye on daughters, traders and women moving on the streets would have only two destinations — “jail or jahannum”.CM Yogi described Prime Minister Narendra Modi as his role model and said he was an ordinary party worker who would discharge whatever responsibility was assigned to him.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath accuses Samajwadi Party leadership of practising family-centric politics. He also criticises the SP-Congress alliance, claiming it had run into trouble even before the elections because of differences over seat-sharing. He claims Uttar Pradesh has moved from being a 'BIU' state to a growth engine.

Article Title: Karthigai Deepam row: Why lighting a lamp has triggered a legal battle in Tamil Nadu
Article Text:

What is the Karthigai Deepam row?

What did the Supreme Court order on November 20

What happened on November 24

Why did the Madurai collector say the lamp could not be lit at Deepathoon

Opposition slams Tamil Nadu government

NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government apologised before the Supreme Court on Wednesday after the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp was not lit at the designated Deepathoon stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai on November 24, despite the court's interim direction.In a status report filed by Madurai district collector Nishant Krishna, the state government said the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the team proposed to carry out the ritual and instead decided to retain the customary location.The development came after the ceremonial lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple, rather than at Deepathoon, which was the subject of the Supreme Court's November 20 order. The court said it would consider the contempt plea alleging non-compliance with its directions and asked the petitioner and other parties to file appropriate applications.The dispute over the ritual's location has been continuing for years, with Hindu groups seeking permission to light the lamp at the hilltop stone pillar near the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah, while the state government and temple authorities have maintained that the customary venue is near the Ucchi Pillayar temple.Also read| ‘Lamp could not be lit at designated spot’: Tamil Nadu govt apologises in Supreme Court, contempt plea to be heard in Karthigai Deepam row The November 24 ceremony, the subsequent explanation by the district administration and the demand for contempt proceedings have now brought the dispute back before the Supreme Court.Karthigai Deepam is a traditional Tamil Hindu festival celebrated by lighting lamps in homes and temples. At Thiruparankundram, the dispute concerns the location where the ceremonial lamp, or Maha Deepam, should be lit during the annual festival.For decades, the lamp has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes of Thiruparankundram hill. However, Hindu groups have sought permission to light it at Deepathoon, a stone pillar located higher up the hill and around 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah.The disagreement is not limited to the ritual's location. It also involves competing claims over the stone pillar's character and the hilltop's ownership and status. While Hindu groups describe Deepathoon as an ancient structure associated with the ritual, another side argues that it is a survey stone. The dargah committee has also contested the demand, claiming ownership of the hilltop.The dispute has travelled through the courts over several years. In December 2025, a single judge of the Madras High Court directed the temple authorities to light the lamp at Deepathoon. A division bench upheld the direction in its January 6, 2026, judgment. The state government subsequently challenged the High Court's decision before the Supreme Court.The Tamil Nadu government and the temple administration have maintained that the lamp has traditionally been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple. The state has also raised concerns over the legal and administrative implications of allowing the ritual at the disputed pillar, including the possibility of law-and-order complications because of its proximity to the dargah.On November 20, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi permitted the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time interim arrangement. The order came while the Supreme Court was hearing challenges to the Madras High Court's directions on the ritual.The court allowed only a restricted team authorised by the temple administration and government officials to go to the location and carry out the ceremony. It also designated the district collector as the nodal officer responsible for coordination and supervision.The Supreme Court imposed safeguards to prevent any escalation at the disputed site. It restrained members of the public from going to the location and prohibited processions, public gatherings, slogan-raising and demonstrations during the ceremony. The court also stayed portions of the Madras High Court judgment that had upheld the direction to restore the practice of lighting the lamp at Deepathoon.Importantly, the permission was limited to November 24 and did not settle the larger dispute over the ritual's history, the hilltop's ownership, or any customary or religious right to light the lamp at the pillar. The court clarified that neither the permission nor the ceremony could be treated as proof of an established custom or a continuing right of access to the location.The Tamil Nadu government subsequently approached the Supreme Court seeking a review of the November 20 order and a stay on the one-time permission. However, the interim direction remained the basis for the November 24 arrangements.The Karthigai Deepam ceremony took place amid heightened security and tension at Thiruparankundram on November 24. However, the lamp was not lit at Deepathoon, the location specified by the Supreme Court. Instead, the Maha Deepam was lit at the customary Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple at around 6 pm.The development came hours after Madurai collector Nishant Krishna told the Madurai bench of the Madras High Court that the Supreme Court's directions would be implemented. The High Court had also reminded officials of their responsibility to comply with the apex court's order and warned of contempt proceedings in the event of non-compliance.State law minister C T R Nirmalkumar confirmed the lighting at the customary location in a post on X, saying: "Karthigai Mahadeepam has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near Ucchi Pillaiyar temple, directly above the sanctum sanctorum of the presiding deity at Thiruparankundram".The decision triggered protests by Hindu organisations and BJP workers, who demanded that the government implement the Supreme Court's direction. Tensions were reported near the hill, where protesters raised slogans against the state government. Police had deployed more than 5,600 personnel in Thiruparankundram and adjoining areas, with restrictions imposed on public access to the hilltop.The district administration later said that the last-minute decision to retain the customary venue followed concerns raised by the temple's Board of Trustees. The trustees maintained that the Deepa Mandapam was the traditional location for the ritual and that the practice should continue there.In a status report filed before the Supreme Court, Madurai district collector Nishant Krishna said the administration had made arrangements to implement the November 20 order but could not proceed because the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the team proposed to light the lamp.According to the district administration's explanation, the Supreme Court had designated the collector as the coordinating officer, while the temple administration was responsible for authorising the personnel who would carry out the ritual. The administration said it had completed the necessary arrangements, but the trustees eventually resolved to retain the customary location.The Board of Trustees cited religious traditions and established worship practices in support of its decision. It maintained that the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple was the customary venue and that the location was directly above the head of Lord Murugan, the presiding deity. The trustees also referred to Agama rules governing temple rituals and festivals.In its statement after the ceremony, the district administration said: "The trustees unanimously resolved to retain the customary venue, citing religious traditions and established worship practices."The trustees said their decision followed an examination of historical and religious records and consultations with the temple's Sthanikars, or hereditary ritual functionaries. They also decided to place their findings before the court.The collector apologised for the failure to light the lamp at Deepathoon and maintained that the administration had made every effort to comply with the Supreme Court's direction. The state's position was that the district administration could not independently authorise another team to perform the ritual in the absence of the temple Board of Trustees' approval.The status report also maintained that there had been no wilful or deliberate disobedience of the Supreme Court's directions. The government said the failure to carry out the ceremony at the designated location was due to the trustees' decision to retain the customary venue.The failure to light the lamp at Deepathoon led to demands for contempt proceedings against the state authorities. The petitioner seeking permission for the ritual alleged that the government had failed to comply with the Supreme Court's November 20 direction despite assurances given before the Madras High Court that the order would be implemented.During Wednesday's proceedings, a senior advocate appearing for the petitioner termed the developments "most unfortunate". He argued that the flame should have been carried to Deepathoon and the lamp lit there, and alleged deliberate non-compliance with the apex court's directions.The counsel also urged the Supreme Court to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings against the authorities concerned. When the senior advocate indicated that the petitioners would move a contempt plea, the bench said, "File it, and then we will see."The Supreme Court asked the petitioner and other parties to file appropriate applications and said it would hear the matter. The bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi also said it would peruse the status report filed by the state government.The contempt allegation centres on whether the authorities failed to implement the Supreme Court's specific direction despite the district administration being tasked with coordinating the ceremony. The state government, however, has denied wilful disobedience and attributed the failure to the temple trustees' decision not to authorise the proposed team.The Supreme Court's consideration of the contempt plea will therefore bring the conduct of the officials and the explanation submitted by the district administration under judicial scrutiny.The failure to light the lamp at Deepathoon has triggered sharp criticism from BJP leaders, who have accused the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government of disregarding the Supreme Court's interim order and hurting the sentiments of devotees.BJP national general secretary B L Santhosh accused the state government of defying the court's directions and said the government would face a "civilisational and legal challenge". In a post on X, he alleged that the Madurai district administration had lit the lamp at the Ucchi Pillayar Mandapam instead of the Deepathoon stone pillar as directed by the Supreme Court.Also read| ‘Crores of devotees let down’: BJP slams Vijay govt for defying SC order on Deepam row In another post, Santhosh accused the government of compromising the sentiments of devotees to accommodate its political allies. He said: "You people have hurt devotes & defied SC Order to please some alliance partners & you yourself is Law Minister of a Govt which will fully defied SC Order . To please some friends you let down crores of devotees," he alleged.Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran also accused the state government and district administration of failing to implement the court's order. He criticised the decision to light the lamp at the customary location after the collector had assured the Madras High Court that the Supreme Court's direction would be followed."Lighting the lamp at the Pillaiyar temple after assuring the court that arrangements were being made is an act of deception. It is akin to fooling a child with candy, and they are attempting to deceive the Supreme Court and High Court judges," Nagenthran said.BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan also accused the government of violating the interim order and alleged that the decision was taken to appease its alliance partners. She questioned why the government had not raised its objections based on Agama rules before the Supreme Court.The BJP's criticism came alongside protests by Hindu organisations in different parts of Tamil Nadu. Demonstrations were reported in Ramanathapuram and Pollachi, where protesters demanded that the government comply with the Supreme Court's direction. Police detained protesters involved in road blockades, while cases were registered against members of BJP and Hindu organisations over the demonstrations.The state government and temple trustees, however, have defended the decision to retain the customary location, citing religious traditions and established worship practices.
Article Summary: Karthigai Deepam is a traditional Tamil Hindu festival celebrated by lighting lamps in homes and temples. At Thiruparankundram, the dispute concerns the location where the ceremonial lamp, or Maha Deepam, should be lit during the annual festival. Hindu groups have sought permission to light it at Deepathoon, a stone pillar located higher up the hill and around 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah. The dispute has travelled through the courts over several years.

NEW DELHI: A court on Wednesday sentenced three BJP-RSS workers to life imprisonment for the 2016 murder of CPM activist CV Dhanaraj in Kannur district.The court also imposed a fine of Rs 5 lakh on each of the convicts.Taliparamba Additional Sessions Judge KN Prashanth had found TP Biju (34), M Vipin (34) and M Vaishakh (31), who are brothers, guilty of the murder on November 23. The court acquitted 16 other accused in the case.The three convicts were sentenced to life imprisonment under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The court directed that the total fine of Rs 15 lakh be paid to Dhanaraj's family, particularly his wife and mother.They were also awarded a total of five years and four months of imprisonment each under various other IPC sections, including Sections 447, 323 and 506(II).Special Public Prosecutor CK Sreedharan said the life sentences would begin after the convicts complete their prison terms. They would also face additional imprisonment if they fail to pay the fines.Speaking to reporters, Sreedharan said the prosecution was satisfied with the quantum of punishment but would challenge the acquittal of the 16 accused, particularly those allegedly involved in the conspiracy.The court did not consider the case to fall under the 'rarest of rare' category that warrants the death penalty. However, it observed that the murder was a planned and deliberate act, even though the prosecution failed to establish the charge of criminal conspiracy under Section 120B of the IPC.Sreedharan said the prosecution had presented evidence against certain individuals allegedly involved in the conspiracy and would study the 147-page judgment before deciding on further legal action.The court also directed the District Legal Services Authority to assess the financial condition of Dhanaraj's family and consider providing them additional assistance.What happened in the 2016 murderDhanaraj, the CPM branch secretary at Ezhimala, was hacked to death on July 11, 2016, while returning home at Ramanthali near Payyannur.According to the prosecution, a group of assailants followed him on motorcycles and attacked him with sharp weapons near his house. He was hacked and stabbed to death in front of his mother and wife.A total of 20 BJP-RSS workers were named as accused in the case. However, the trial was completed against only 19, as the 12th accused, C Biju, also known as Churakkattu Biju, was later murdered.The trial began on September 25, 2025. The court examined 43 witnesses, while the prosecution produced 177 documents and 33 material exhibits.The case was initially investigated by V Ramesan, the then Payyannur Circle Inspector. The investigation was later completed by MP Asad, who filed the chargesheet.The murder case had recently returned to the political spotlight after former CPM district committee member V Kunhikrishnan alleged irregularities in the collection of funds raised in the name of Dhanaraj's martyrdom.Kunhikrishnan was subsequently expelled from the party and later won the Payyannur Assembly seat as an independent candidate backed by the Congress-led UDF.
Article Summary: Court sentences three BJP-RSS workers to life imprisonment for the 2016 murder of CPM activist CV Dhanaraj. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 5 lakh on each of the convicts. TP Biju (34), M Vipin (34) and M Vaishakh (31), who are brothers, were found guilty of the murder on November 23.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Wednesday moved the Delhi high court after immigration authorities stopped him from boarding a flight to London over alleged discrepancies in his passport details, particularly his place of birth.Das was scheduled to travel to the United Kingdom for a series of engagements, including a panel discussion organised by the Oxford Union on December 1. His passport was flagged by immigration authorities at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on Tuesday, preventing him from travelling.The development followed a show-cause notice issued to Das by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai, on Monday evening, asking him to explain alleged discrepancies in his birth-related documents within seven days. The notice warned that his passport could be impounded under the Passports Act, 1967, if he failed to provide a satisfactory explanation.According to government sources, inconsistencies in details such as his date of birth and father's name were flagged across documents, including his Aadhaar card, passport and school certificate. The authorities initiated a fresh verification of his documents and information recorded in his passport application.The passport was originally issued to Das on August 21, 2019, following the verification process.According to government officials, a passport holder issued a show-cause notice over allegedly incorrect particulars cannot use the passport for international travel until the matter is resolved.An official told TOI, "As per rules, if a show-cause notice is issued to the passport holder on why his passport should not be impounded in view of furnishing of incorrect particulars, and a reply is awaited, the respondent cannot travel abroad on that passport till the matter is disposed of."Another government officer said Das had time until November 30 to respond to the notice. The official added that he could resume international travel using the same passport once the RPO completed its re-verification and cleared the documents.However, Das said he became aware of the notice only after reaching the airport, claiming that it had been issued just hours before his scheduled departure.Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Das questioned the timing of the notice and the discrepancies flagged by the authorities, pointing out that his passport had been issued in 2019 after police verification and that he had undertaken several international trips since then.“How was I issued the passport which was given after police verification?” he asked.Alleging that the action was linked to his association with the CJP, Das said, “I was scheduled to talk in various prestigious universities in London on their invitation. That trip couldn’t be completed because the coward govt has flagged my passport citing some discrepancies...”Apart from the Oxford Union panel discussion, Das said he was scheduled to participate in engagements involving Cambridge University, the London School of Economics and the University of Edinburgh.The Oxford Union event was scheduled for December 1, with Das and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke listed as key panellists on the organisation's website.Explaining the purpose of his proposed engagements, Das said he intended to discuss the growth of the CJP movement and its use of non-violent methods.“The Indian students studying there wanted to understand what CJP movement is and how it grew. I would have spoken about how this movement without violence could become successful. How the world’s Gen Z could learn from us,” he said.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh, who was also scheduled to travel to the UK, said her visa had been rejected a few days earlier. Dipke said he had also received an invitation but was scheduled to attend a CJP programme in Nagpur on November 26, coinciding with Constitution Day.The London School of Economics Students' Union Amnesty International Society subsequently announced that its event featuring Das had been indefinitely postponed. In a statement, it condemned what it described as an “arbitrary obstruction” and the “apparent targeting of an individual seeking to engage in academic dialogue and public discussion”.The society expressed solidarity with Das and said it would share updates if the event could be rescheduled.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned the decision to stop Das from travelling, drawing comparisons with the cases of fugitive economic offenders Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi.“Is he (Das) a terrorist, a criminal? Why was he stopped?” Dipke asked at a separate press conference.Meanwhile, a public interest litigation has also been filed in the Madras High Court concerning alleged inconsistencies in Das's birth and parentage documents, while also questioning his citizenship.The passport authorities' re-verification process is pending, with Das required to respond to the show-cause notice by November 30.
Article Summary: CJP co-convener Saurav Das moved the Delhi high court after immigration authorities stopped him from boarding a flight to London. Das was scheduled to travel to the United Kingdom for a series of engagements, including a panel discussion organised by the Oxford Union. His passport was flagged by immigration authorities at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on Tuesday, preventing him from travelling.

BENGALURU: The Supreme Court on Wednesday cancelled the bail granted to former Congress MLA Vinay Kulkarni in the 2016 murder of BJP worker and Dharwad zilla panchayat member Yogeshgouda Goudar, setting aside the Karnataka High Court’s July 31, 2026 order that suspended his life sentence and stayed his conviction.The apex court’s decision withdraws the relief granted by the high court while Kulkarni’s criminal appeal was pending. The high court had ordered his release on bail after suspending the life sentence imposed by a special court for elected representatives.Kulkarni and 16 others were convicted of murder and criminal conspiracy in the case. The special court sentenced all 17 to life imprisonment after finding them guilty of plotting and executing Goudar’s killing.Goudar, a BJP zilla panchayat member, was hacked to death at a gym in Saptapur, Dharwad, on June 15, 2016. The local police initially investigated the case, which was transferred to the Central Bureau of Investigation in 2019 after allegations of political pressure and claims that Kulkarni, then a district in-charge minister, had orchestrated the killing.The CBI arrested Kulkarni on Nov 5, 2020, naming him the main conspirator.The Supreme Court granted him conditional bail on Aug 11, 2021, with a restriction on entering Dharwad district. It cancelled that bail on June 7, 2025, after allegations of attempts to influence or tamper with witnesses.The apex court granted Kulkarni bail again on Feb 27, 2026, after key witnesses had been examined and directed that the trial be concluded expeditiously. He was convicted along with the other accused on April 15, 2026, and all 17 were sentenced to life imprisonment on April 17.With the Supreme Court now setting aside the high court’s July 31 order, the suspension of Kulkarni’s conviction and life sentence no longer holds. The conviction and sentence will continue to operate, subject to the outcome of his appeal.
Article Summary: Kulkarni and 16 others were convicted of murder and criminal conspiracy in the case. Karnataka High Court’s July 31, 2026 order that suspended his life sentence and stayed his conviction. Goudar, a BJP zilla panchayat member, was hacked to death at a gym in Saptapur, Dharwad.
